main_body: Japanese-style townhouse: a large blue-grey tile roof slope with ridge, a cream plaster band, a lower eave roof, and a wooden lattice facade with a dark central doorway
top_band: Ridge cap rows 1-5 (L 158/130/83) and the tile roof slope rows 7-29 (L 83-158 tile pattern). It is separated from the front face by the eave shadow rows 30-32 (L 46), then the cream wall at rows 33-40 (L 221).
evidence: The roof slope is a large, tiled surface seen from above, similar to the reference house roofs. The scan shows a clear step from roof (L 56-158) through a dark eave shadow (rows 30-32) to the light plaster wall (L 221). A second lower eave roof (rows 41-47) sits over the lattice facade. The doorway is drawn inset and dark, and the lattice bars have dark gaps. The roof reads as a surface and the wall as a vertical face, so the contract is met.

style.evidence: The roof tiles use about 5 steps, which is decent, and flat-fill coverage is only 3%. But 72% of the dark edge pixels are neutral (#231d28 outline), against 7-9% for the references, so the outline reads as a uniform dark sticker line instead of a tinted material tone. Distinct colours are 34 against 66 and 185, and median colours per tile are 8 against 11 and 18. The plaster band and dark facade are simple, and the lattice is regular, repeated bars with little grain. Overall the piece is thinner than the references.
